title: Local History Uncovering Forgotten
author: T JHEL
description:
Whispers from the Hollows: Forgotten Legends of Appalachia and the Pine Barrens
Short Description (for platform listings):
Three quiet legends that never made the history books — a road where cars roll uphill under the hands of Civil War ghosts, a demolished coal-camp house that once held a crying woman and a headless man, and the 300-year-old scream of the Jersey Devil.
Full Episode Description / Show Notes:
In a quiet stretch of road outside Burkittsville, Maryland, drivers still pull over at night, shift into neutral, and feel their cars begin to roll uphill. Locals say the ghosts of Confederate soldiers are still pushing.
In the New River Gorge of West Virginia, Company House Number 24 once stood in the vanished coal camp of Red Star. A family moved in during the 1930s and heard a woman crying, a baby wailing, and footsteps that belonged to a headless man. The company eventually tore the house down. The stories stayed.
And in the vast Pine Barrens of southern New Jersey, something with leathery wings and a horse-like head has been reported for nearly three centuries.
This episode of Local History travels the back roads of three places most people only pass through, uncovering the quieter legends that official history left behind.

One key subject is dysregulation mood disorder, explored through an educational discussion of disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD), a condition associated with persistent irritability and frequent, intense temper outbursts in children and adolescents. The series helps listeners understand the difference between typical childhood frustration and ongoing difficulties that interfere with everyday life, relationships, and school experiences.

The podcast also discusses the importance of early assessment, supportive parenting approaches, therapeutic interventions, and individualized care. By presenting information in a respectful, nonjudgmental manner, Clearer Minds, Stronger Lives aims to help families feel better informed and more prepared to seek appropriate support from qualified healthcare professionals.

A weekly journey into the depth and precision of Rashi’s commentary on the Torah.

Whenever Rashi quotes or references a verse from elsewhere in Tanach, we follow that reference back to its original context and study Rashi’s commentary there as well. By placing these Rashis side by side—comparing language, context, and interpretation—we allow Rashi to illuminate Rashi.

Through this intertextual approach, we uncover connections across Torah and Tanach, clarify difficult passages, compare and contrast seemingly different explanations, and address apparent contradictions within Rashi.

Rather than studying each Rashi in isolation, we seek to see the larger picture: how Rashi’s commentary in one place can unlock his meaning somewhere else.

Each weekly episode focuses on the Parsha and explores how Rashi’s own words throughout Tanach can deepen our understanding of his commentary on the Torah.

title: Not Another Curbside: Training the Mind Behind the Medicine
author: MindShift MD | Chase Yonce, MD, Michele Demetriou, and Taylor Harris MD
description:
You know the curbside. You’re already behind, trying to get some lunch, and someone catches you in the hallway. Got a second?
Well, this is Not Another Curbside and it’s the conversation you’d actually choose to have. Two practicing physicians and a coach who works with professional athletes, CEOs, and high performers sit down each week with a quote or idea - from a legendary coach, an athlete, a thought leader, or occasionally Taylor’s grandfather - and break it down, test it against real life in medicine, and land on something you can use as a physician whenever you need it. Along the way, someone will probably invoke Michael Jordan, an epic movie, or the hip mobility of an NFL quarterback. It usually makes sense by the end.
This is for the doctor who doesn’t want more tips on managing burnout or another physician wellness module.
The premise is simple: the next level of physician performance is mental.
Medical training prepared you to diagnose, decide, and take care of everyone else. What it neglected to teach you is how to manage your own mind - when a case goes sideways, a patient is angry, the schedule implodes, or you’re home but your brain is still at work. That’s what Fierce Mind Management is: physician coaching meets mental performance training. Learning to respond instead of react. Pursuing excellence without demanding perfection. Treating a miss as information rather than a verdict. And managing your energy so the people at home get you, not what’s left of you.
Taylor (orthopedic surgery) and Chase (family medicine) are still in the trenches - still operating, still in clinic, and still making the most of every challenge. Michele has built a career coaching professional athletes, CEOs, and is bringing the same framework to medicine.
No doubt, medicine is a difficult field to succeed in. There will always be challenges, and a better mindset won’t cancel call. But how you meet pressure, recover from a miss, lead your team, and decide what an outcome means about you… that part can be trained and WILL make you a better physician.
No one gets great in isolation, even if medicine acts like you should. Come for the conversation. Stay for the brotherhood. Your lunch is already cold anyway.
Tune in if you’ve ever found yourself asking:
~ Why can’t I stop thinking about that case?
~ Why doesn’t time off fix physician burnout?
~ Is work-life balance actually possible for doctors?
~ How do I say no without feeling like I’m failing everyone?
~ Who am I when the white coat comes off?

author: 𝐌𝐀𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐈̇𝐂𝐊® @trendexplorer
description:
Global Compass” is a podcast series dedicated to exploring the complex and ever-evolving tapestry of cultural, societal, and political dynamics shaping our world today. In a time where the world feels more interconnected yet increasingly divided, “Global Compass” serves as your guide through the intricacies of global affairs, offering insights and analyses that go beyond the headlines. Each episode is a deep dive into the stories, cultures, and events that shape our societies, revealing the underlying currents that influence how people live, think, and interact in different parts of the world.
At “Global Compass,” we believe that understanding the world requires a multifaceted approach—one that considers the historical, cultural, and social contexts that give rise to today’s pressing issues. Our episodes focus on the intersection of these forces, uncovering the narratives that shape nations, communities, and individuals. From exploring the cultural traditions that define a society’s identity to analyzing the global impacts of political decisions, we aim to provide a holistic view that connects the dots between seemingly unrelated events and trends.
In today’s fast-paced world, global issues often feel overwhelming, and understanding the ‘why’ behind them can be a daunting task. That’s where “Global Compass” steps in. We go beyond the surface to offer our listeners thoughtful and in-depth discussions, featuring expert interviews, firsthand accounts, and stories from people living through the events we cover. By listening to those directly impacted and incorporating expert analysis, we bridge the gap between local realities and global narratives, presenting a well-rounded perspective on critical issues.
The topics we cover span a broad range—from the politics that shape international relations to the social movements redefining community and identity. We dive into the cultural phenomena that bring people together and the divides that separate us. Whether it’s examining the economic policies of a powerful nation or understanding the impact of migration on local communities, “Global Compass” ensures each episode is both informative and thought-provoking, encouraging our audience to question, learn, and grow.
Each episode of “Global Compass” is meticulously crafted to engage, educate, and inspire. We use storytelling as a powerful tool to make complex subjects accessible and relatable. Our host guides listeners on a journey through history, geography, and culture, weaving narratives that reveal the interconnectedness of events and the ripple effects they have across borders. From the rise of new global powers to the impact of climate change on societies, we explore the challenges and opportunities that define the 21st century.
“Global Compass” also recognizes the importance of inclusivity and diversity in understanding the global landscape. Our episodes feature voices from a wide range of backgrounds, including journalists, historians, activists, and everyday people, to provide a comprehensive view of the issues at hand. By amplifying diverse perspectives, we aim to challenge preconceived notions and expand the conversation beyond conventional narratives.
Moreover, our show is not just about understanding the present; it’s about exploring the future. We look ahead to emerging trends and consider the potential paths societies may take. Whether discussing the future of technology and its impact on privacy, the role of youth movements in reshaping democracies, or the evolution of global economies, “Global Compass” offers insights that prepare listeners for the world to come.

Hacking Your Cyber Career


Real advice. Real experience. Your next move.

Thinking about a career in cybersecurity but not sure where to start? Already working in cyber and wondering how to take that next step?

Welcome to Hacking Your Cyber Career, the podcast that helps you break into cybersecurity, get ahead, and build a career worth having.

Hosted by Steve, a former CISO and cybersecurity executive with over 30 years of IT experience, this show takes you behind the scenes of what it really takes to succeed in the industry.

We'll explore everything from choosing the right career path and landing your first job to navigating interviews, building technical skills, earning certifications, getting promoted, and eventually moving into leadership.

Along the way, Steve shares lessons from his own career, insights from years of hiring and developing cybersecurity professionals, and the things employers actually look for but rarely tell you.

Expect practical advice, honest conversations, real world stories, and a healthy dose of British humor.

No hype. No shortcuts to six figure salaries. And definitely no promises that collecting certifications will magically land you a job.

You're not behind, you're in the making.

title: Anti-Aging & Plastic Surgery with Dr. Dan Gould
author: Dan
description:
Your jawline is softening, your neck is starting to sag, and the creams, the devices and the filler aren't fixing it. That's because it isn't a skin problem. It's structural.


This podcast is for women in their 40s and 50s who want to look like themselves again, not like they've had work done. I break down what really happens to a face as it ages, what a deep plane facelift and a deep neck lift actually do, and when treatments like filler, lasers and radiofrequency are worth your money and when they aren't.


Most surgeons treat facial aging as a skin and volume problem. I think the real problem is deeper. Ligaments loosen, tissue drops, and you can't fill your way out of that. So I treat the patient in front of me, not whatever's trending.


I'm Dr. Dan Gould, a board-certified plastic surgeon in Beverly Hills with a PhD in bioengineering.


Consults are in Beverly Hills, California.

description:

From the first dinosaurs to the asteroid that ended them, from the Cambrian explosion to the feathered dinosaurs of China, from the woolly mammoth to the dream of bringing it back, Fossil is about deep time — the vast, strange history written in stone, and the patient human effort to read it. Meticulously researched, honest about what is known and what is debated. Clean and suitable for all ages. A new fossil every week.

Here you'll find answers to the questions people actually ask before full mouth dental implants. Who's a candidate and who isn't. What severe bone loss really means. What dentures can and can't do. title: Solve For...
author: Nova Institute for Health
description:
What would it mean to create a world where health is valued as our most essential asset? A future where people, places, and our planet can truly flourish? Sometimes, all it takes is a tiny change, a local fix, or a spark of innovation to help us think differently. Solve For... is all about finding those emerging possibilities and embracing the power of curiosity to bring health and well-being into focus in unexpected new ways. 
Join acclaimed journalist Kate Morgan and Nova Institute for Health president Brian Berman, MD, as they highlight the innovators tackling solutions to our most complex challenges at the intersection of medicine, biology, neuroscience, nutrition, the arts, and more. 
In an era of overwhelm, change doesn't have to be huge to be meaningful. It just has to start somewhere.
Hosts: 
Kate Morgan is a freelance journalist based in Pennsylvania. Her reporting has appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, National Geographic, BBC, Popular Science, Sierra, and many other publications. Kate's work takes a broad view of health and often focuses on the inherent optimism of those working to repair and restore natural ecosystems and human communities.
Brian Berman, MD, is the president of the Nova Institute for Health, which he founded in 2007 to catalyze new ideas in health. He is professor emeritus at the University of Maryland School of Medicine, where he was the director of the Center for Integrative Medicine. Dr. Berman has served as an advisor to the NIH, chairing and subsequently serving for three terms on the advisory committee to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. He cofounded and, for 25 years, directed the complementary medicine field of Cochrane, an internationally recognized leader in evidence-based medicine. Dr. Berman is also the recipient of the prestigious Bravewell Leadership Award, which celebrates and supports visionaries who have committed their medical careers to transforming health care in America.
Solve For...is a production of the Nova Institute for Health. Written and produced by Kate Morgan. Editing and sound design by Olanre Adewole. Executive producers: Brian Berman and Sue Berman. To learn more, visit novainstituteforhealth.org.

description:
Wellness Without Wine with Deirdre Coyne

What if life could feel better without wine at the centre of it?

Welcome to Wellness Without Wine, a podcast for women who want to rethink their relationship with alcohol and discover a healthier, happier and more fulfilling way to live.

I'm Deirdre Coyne, a Sober Coach and Positive Psychology Coach. Drawing on psychology, mindset and behaviour change, I'll explore why we reach for wine, how everyday habits become part of our lives, and how we can begin to make different choices.

Together, we'll look at the role alcohol can play in stress, switching off, confidence, emotional wellbeing and our sense of identity. We'll explore practical strategies to help you understand your habits, reconnect with what matters to you and create more of the things you want in life.

Expect honest conversations, bite-sized podshots, practical reflections and deeper dives into the psychology of change.

This isn't about judgement or perfection. It's about curiosity, self-understanding and discovering what life could look like when you start putting your own wellbeing first.

Because this isn't just about drinking less or living without wine. It's about creating a life you genuinely enjoy.

Wellness Without Wine — a fresh perspective on alcohol, mindset and your next chapter.

Now, we’re taking you beyond the warehouse floor to explore the ideas, technologies, and people shaping the next century of lift trucks and logistics. 


Each episode, we:


• Break down the latest in drivetrain, battery, safety, and automation technologies
• Talk with industry experts, operators, and leaders who keep supply chains running
• Unpack real-world applications, operational insights, and lessons learned from the field
• Explore how efficiency, safety, and sustainability are redefining the way the world moves 


From legacy engineering to next-generation innovation, Between The Forks brings you an inside look at the evolution of an industry CLARK helped create — and continues to lead.  Whether you manage a fleet, move materials, or simply want to understand the machinery that powers the global economy, this is your inside track to the world that moves the world.
